message.content:
**Mating Process of Lions (Panthera leo)** | Stage | Key Behaviors & Details | |-------|------------------------| | **Courtship & Selection** | • Male lions typically live in coalitions (usually 2–5 individuals).
• They patrol territories and use scent marking, roaring, and visual displays (mane erection) to attract females.
• Females (lionesses) are polyestrous; they come into estrus roughly once a year, lasting 2–3 days.
• During estrus, females emit pheromones that signal receptivity. Males may engage in “licking” or gentle touching of the female’s flank to stimulate her. | | **Mate Guarding** | • Once a male detects a receptive female, he will guard her against rival males.
• Guarding can involve physical proximity, vocalizing, and sometimes fighting other males. | | **Copulation** | • When the female is ready, the male mounts from behind.
• He grips her with his forepaws and holds on for several minutes (average 1–2 minutes).
• Multiple males may mate with the same female during a single estrus cycle, leading to sperm competition. | | **Gestation** | • After successful fertilization, the female’s gestation lasts about 110 days (~3.5 months).
• She gives birth in a den, usually at night, to a litter of 1–4 cubs. | | **Post‑birth** | • Lionesses raise the cubs alone; male lions do not participate in rearing.
• Cubs stay with their mother until they are 2–3 years old before dispersing. | **Key Points** * Male lions rely heavily on dominance and coalition dynamics to secure mating opportunities. * Female estrus is brief, so timing is critical; males often mate multiple times within a single estrus to increase chances of fertilization. * Sperm competition among males is common, as multiple males may mate with the same female. * Lionesses are the sole caregivers; male lions leave the pride after reaching sexual maturity (~2–3 years).
